cl_benzo_harm_reduction_services.q: Which harm reduction services exist for benzos, and do they work?
cl_benzo_harm_reduction_services.short: Drug checking, prescribed benzos and stricter rules exist. No study has shown whether they lower harm.
cl_benzo_harm_reduction_services.but: The review did not judge how good the studies were, and most had no comparison group.
how: A 2025 review found 35 reports on harm reduction for benzos.

About half of the drug-checking reports tested how well testing machines find drugs. A portable machine found the designer benzo etizolam in 36 of 100 samples that had it; an infrared machine found it in 9.
At one service in Canada, people brought 139 samples they thought were Xanax. An infrared machine found alprazolam, the drug in Xanax, in 33 of them.
Studies of benzos on prescription and of stricter rules could not show what caused what. Their results were mixed.

freq.what: samples that people thought were Xanax had alprazolam in them, by infrared testing
freq.note: 33 of 139 samples at one Canadian drug-checking service, as reported in a 2025 review.

cl_opi_using_alone.q: Why do people use drugs alone, and does it matter for overdose?
cl_opi_using_alone.short: About 3 in 4 people at harm reduction sites had used alone that week. The top reason was comfort at home.
cl_opi_using_alone.but: It was one survey in one part of Canada. Everyone asked already went to these sites.
how: In 2018, 414 people at 27 sites in British Columbia, Canada, did a short survey. The sites hand out safer-use supplies.
Of those who used alone, 44 in 100 said using at home was easier and more comfortable; 14 in 100 did not want others to know. Some wrote that they had no one to use with.
People who used alone were more often without a steady home than people who did not.
The survey could not show if using alone changes overdose risk. It cites coroners' reports. They found that about 7 in 10 people who died of an overdose there in 2016 and 2017 were using alone.

freq.what: had used drugs alone at least once in the past week
freq.note: 314 of 414 people at 27 harm reduction sites in British Columbia, Canada, in 2018.

cl_can_cbd_with_thc.q: Does CBD taken with THC change THC's effects?
cl_can_cbd_with_thc.short: In one lab trial, THC eaten with a lot of CBD felt more unpleasant, not less.
cl_can_cbd_with_thc.but: Just one small trial. It used a large amount of CBD, and other test medicines too.
how: 18 healthy adults who had not used cannabis for at least a month each ate three brownies, on different days. One was a dummy, one had THC, and one had the same THC plus a large amount of CBD.
With CBD, the amount of THC in their blood went almost twice as high.
They felt the drug more, felt sicker, had more trouble with memory and simple tasks, and their hearts beat faster. They did not like it more.
Other test medicines, including a sedative, were given each time. They may have added to the effects.
